claims.claim: The chart's length rows are Foot Length (in) and (cm); the CM size on boxes and labels is not the foot length.
claims.exact_words: Find your size in the chart below. If you do not know your size, use the How To Measure Foot Length prompts at the bottom of the size guide to help you find the right size. Please note the CM size displayed on shoe boxes and labels is different than Foot Length (cm).

claims.claim: Helper marks big toe tip and outermost heel on taped paper, weight even; the distance is the foot length; take the longer foot; between sizes, size up.
claims.exact_words: With a pen or pencil pointed straight down, have a friend or partner assist you by marking the tip of the big toe and the outermost part of the heel. Once the marks are recorded, step off the paper and use a ruler or measuring tape to measure the distance between the two points. This measurement represents the length of the foot. ... Apply the longer of the two measurements to our size chart to find the right correlating size for the recorded foot length. If the measurement is between sizes, we recommend sizing up.
claims.notes: Word for word the method on reebok.com.au (rb-au-measure).

claims.claim: The same method and size-up advice on the women's guide.
claims.exact_words: This measurement represents the length of the foot. ... If the measurement is between sizes, we recommend sizing up.

claims.claim: Measure at day's end; heel lightly against a wall; mark the longest toe; measure wall to mark; both feet; compare with the chart.
claims.exact_words: For the best fit, measure your feet at the end of the day. 1. Step on а piece of paper with your heel slightly touching a wall behind. 2. Мark the end of your longest toe on the paper (you might need a friend to help you) and measure from the wall to the marking. 3. Do the same for the other foot and compare measurements with our size chart to get the right size.
claims.notes: The page's text uses Cyrillic а and М in two words (as printed).

claims.claim: Between sizes: one size down for a tight fit, one size up for a loose fit.
claims.exact_words: IN BETWEEN SIZES? For tight fit, go one size down. For loose fit, go one size up.
claims.notes: Search shows another adidas page saying 'If between sizes, we recommend you order 1/2 size up' (lead; not read).

claims.claim: Measure heel to longest toe in cm, then add 1 to 1.5 cm to get the length to match with the size guide.
claims.exact_words: With the outline, measure a straight line from your heel to the longest toe. This gives you the length of your foot in centimeters. STEP 3 Lastly, add 1-1.5 centimeters to the length. This will give you the correct length to match with our shoe size guide. This extra space gives your feet room to warm up and expand during your run.
claims.notes: So the size guide's CM is not the bare foot length: the rule matches foot + 1 to 1.5 cm to it.

claims.claim: Australia: the same three steps, word for word, adding 1 to 1.5 cm.
claims.exact_words: Step 3 Lastly, add 1-1.5 centimeters to the length. This will give you the correct length to match with our shoe size guide. This extra space gives your feet room to warm up and expand during your run.
claims.notes: Also points to a printable Foot Measurement Tool for Kids.

claims.claim: Singapore's footwear sizing guides: measure in the socks you wear with the shoe, heel to the wall, line just before the big toe, take the longer foot; the chart has FOOT LENGTH (CM) and (INCH) columns.
claims.exact_words: Make sure you are wearing the same socks that you would normally wear with this type of shoe. Wearing these socks, stand on the sheet of paper with your foot perpendicular to the wall and your heel against the wall. Then use a pen to draw a line just before your big toe. Repeat this for both feet and take the longer distance to determine your size. Using a ruler, measure the distance between the wall and the line you drew to find your size.
